- **Water wheel** [`water_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_wheel.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Arno mills grind grain and full cloth; the flood of 1333 swept away the weirs and mills in the city, since rebuilt. Other streams drive paper mills and forges. Local: Arno mills and weirs; fulling mills upstream of the city; paper mills of Fabriano.
- **Windmill** [`windmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Known by sight and from Dante's Inferno, but Tuscany mills by water. A post mill is carpenter's work once the gearing is explained. Elsewhere: Flanders and northern France; Castile; Aegean islands.
- **Water turbine** [`water_turbine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_turbine.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Hill mills use a horizontal wheel (ritrecine) struck by a jet, a crude turbine. Curved guide vanes and a closed casing are unknown. Local: millwrights of the Apennine valleys.
- **Crank, connecting rod and flywheel** [`crank_connecting_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crank_connecting_rod.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Hand cranks turn grindstones and hurdy-gurdies. A connecting rod turning rotation into push and pull, and a flywheel on a crank, are not built anywhere in Europe. Local: carpenters; smiths. Elsewhere: Paris, Guido da Vigevano's manuscript of 1335 draws crank-driven war wagons; Islamic lands, al-Jazari's crank-driven pump (1206).
- **Piston pumps (suction and force pump)** [`piston_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/piston_pump.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept high. Water is raised by buckets, windlasses and wheels of pots. Only the clyster syringe works by a piston; Vitruvius' force pump is a line in rare manuscripts. Local: bronze founders; well diggers and fountain masters. Elsewhere: Islamic lands, al-Jazari's twin-cylinder pump.
- **Hydraulic ram** [`hydraulic_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_ram.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept high. Needs a strong lead or bronze pipe, two valves and an air vessel. Valve making is unfamiliar; pipes burst if the air cushion is forgotten. Local: plumbers (lead pipe); bronze founders; Siena's fountain masters (water reached the Campo in 1343).
- **Charcoal burning** [`charcoal_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charcoal_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Charcoal burners supply every forge and furnace; fuel is the limit on all metalwork. Local: charcoal burners of the Casentino and Mugello; Maremma woods.
- **Deep coal mining (drainage, ventilation, safety lamp)** [`coal_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coal_mining.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept low. Tuscany has wood and only poor lignite. Marco Polo's black stones that burn are a traveller's tale; northern sea coal is distrusted for its smoke. Elsewhere: Liege; Newcastle and London; China, coal as common fuel.

- **Argand lamp (hollow wick and glass chimney)** [`argand_lamp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/argand_lamp.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept high. Olive-oil lamps with a solid wick and tallow candles are universal. Needs a woven tubular wick, a brass burner and a thin glass chimney that survives the heat. Local: glassmakers of Gambassi; brass and copper workers.
- **Drilling for brine, gas and oil** [`oil_drilling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oil_drilling.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Rock oil is a rare drug and an ingredient of incendiaries. Wells are dug, not drilled; Florence's salt comes from the sea and Volterra's brine springs. Local: Volterra salt works. Elsewhere: Sichuan (China), percussion-drilled brine and gas wells; Baku, hand-dug oil pits described by Marco Polo.
- **Steam reaction toy (aeolipile)** [`steam_aeolipile`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steam_aeolipile.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Hero is unknown in the West. Albertus Magnus describes a vessel that blows steam, and Vitruvius' bronze wind-balls sit in rare monastic manuscripts. Local: coppersmiths.
